correctness.rationale: The CRT inclusion-exclusion counts and high-two-adic exact branch give uniform approximation of T(n)/n by c(n)R(oddpart(n)). Finite-prime CRT equidistribution plus a prime-square summable tail establish weak convergence; compact support establishes all positive moments. Largest-prime denominator valuations prove finite-product injectivity; Mertens-type prime reciprocal divergence and a finite-prefix conditional argument prove no atoms; small tail and divergent logarithmic weights prove exact support. Verification script checks representative finite assertions but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The empirical distribution of a natural group-variant counting totient is a motivated extension of pointwise formulas: the theorem identifies the parity-dependent random limit, every positive moment, full topological support and absence of atoms. These are quantitative and structural facts not determined by the previously known pointwise counts or a first mean; the largest-prime valuation lemma resolves a nontrivial continuity question.
